Are you ready to drive advanced mechatronic innovation and deliver hands-on technical expertise across the Nordics region? JBT Marel is looking for a skilled, customer-focused Electrically biased Field Service Engineer to be based out of our Aarhus hub and support our customers across Denmark, the wider Nordic region, and EMEA. In this role, you will install, maintain, troubleshoot, and optimise sophisticated automated food processing and mechatronic systems, ensuring maximum performance, precision, and reliability. This is an exciting opportunity for an engineer who enjoys combining complex multidisciplinary problem-solving with direct customer interaction in a high-impact, international environment.

What You’ll Be Doing

Carry out installation, commissioning, maintenance, and repair activities at customer sites across the Nordics

Troubleshoot complex mechatronic systems—integrating advanced mechanical components, electrical circuits, PLCs, and automation software

Perform preventive maintenance, calibration, and diagnostics to maximise equipment uptime and operational efficiency

Support customers with expert operational, maintenance, and technical guidance

Deliver professional training to client operators and maintenance teams on equipment handling, troubleshooting, and best practices

Prepare accurate service reports, technical documentation, and follow-up recommendations

Identify spare parts requirements and recommend automation or mechatronic upgrades where appropriate

Collaborate closely with internal R&D, engineering, technical support, and project teams to ensure seamless service delivery

You are a hands-on, analytical, and solution-oriented Electrical Engineer who loves travelling, solving sophisticated technical challenges, and building strong client partnerships. You’ll Bring:

Strong multidisciplinary background spanning electrical engineering, with basic mechanical skills. Automation/PLC control experience would be an advantage

A proactive, safety-first, and customer-focused mindset

The ability to work independently, manage priorities, and adapt quickly on-site

Excellent communication and interpersonal skills

Flexibility and enthusiasm for extensive travel across the Nordics

A structured and professional approach to documentation and reporting

Experience & Education

B.Sc. or M.Sc. in Electrical Engineering or similar would be an advantage

Professional experience in field service, industrial automation, robotics, or complex manufacturing environments

Strong practical experience in electrical troubleshooting & sensor integration

Experience within food processing, packaging, or automated industrial machinery is a distinct advantage

Ability to read and interpret complex technical drawings, electrical schematics, and PLC code

Fluent English (written and spoken); proficiency in Danish or another Nordic language is highly advantageous

Valid driving licence and passport required

Travel & Working Environment

Based out of Aarhus, Denmark (with remote/home office flexibility when not travelling)

Travelling to customer sites across Denmark & the Nordics

A dynamic blend of hands-on site work, remote diagnostics, installations, and technical consultations

Opportunity to work at the cutting edge of global food processing and automation technologies

What’s in it for You

A highly technical and autonomous role with regional responsibility anchored in Aarhus

The chance to work with industry-leading mechatronic and automated food processing technologies

Continuous technical training and professional development opportunities

A collaborative, supportive, and engineering-driven team culture

Competitive salary, travel allowances, and comprehensive benefits package

Clear career growth opportunities within a global organisation

Who We Are

JBT Marel is a global leader in food processing technology, delivering innovative solutions that improve efficiency, quality, and sustainability across the food industry.

Interested?

If you’re ready to take on a dynamic mechatronic engineering role rooted in Aarhus and travelling across the Nordics and EMEA, we’d love to hear from you. 🌐 Learn more: www.jbtmarel.com 🔗 LinkedIn: JBT Marel LinkedIn

jobs.occupation: Service Manager Level 1 SCADA & Power Plant Control
jobs.description:
Company Description

Vattenfall is a leading European energy company driving the transition to a sustainable energy system. We have been electrifying industries, powering homes and transforming life through innovation for more than 100 years. We employ around 21 000 people mostly in our core markets in Sweden, Germany, the Netherlands, Denmark, and the UK.

Job Description

Are you an experienced SCADA engineer or technical service lead who wants to remain hands-on while taking responsibility for reliable service delivery? Would you like to combine solving technical problems with guiding colleagues and improving business-critical services supporting renewable energy?

As our new Service Manager Level 1 SCADA & Power Plant Control, you will be responsible for the reliable, secure and efficient delivery of agreed SCADA and Power Plant Control services supporting Vattenfall’s renewable-energy operations. Your scope includes WTG and substation SCADA, hybrid park controllers and interfaces to WTG Power Plant Controllers.

You will combine hands-on SCADA engineering and incident resolution with functional leadership of a dedicated service team of Level 1 SCADA and Power Plant Control engineers. Alongside your own technical assignments, you will prioritise the team’s work, coordinate suppliers and support functions, and drive continual improvement while meeting agreed service levels.

Working closely with customers, stakeholders and the Asset Service Area OT O&M Manager, you will help develop standardised, proactive service delivery that combines effective incident response with preventive maintenance, lifecycle planning and long-term service improvement.

Be in your element with BA Wind

As part of BA Wind you will play a key role in one of the most exciting pipelines in the industry with 24GW of capacity stretching out more than a decade ahead across our key European markets.

You won’t only be involved in developing projects but pioneering cutting-edge innovation, new business models and ways of working with communities and the environment. Working as part of a leading European utility also means you could be helping a growing number of major businesses and brands achieve their own sustainability goals through partnerships.

Qualifications

Y****our role

You will take responsibility for the delivery and performance of the services within your agreed scope, from their introduction into operation through ongoing support, improvement and eventual replacement or retirement.

Your service scope covers Level 1 SCADA for WTGs and substations, together with assigned Power Plant Control systems and interfaces, including hybrid park controllers and interfaces to WTG Power Plant Controllers. You will take responsibility for their operational support, controlled changes, lifecycle management and continual improvement within agreed ownership boundaries.

This role combines hands-on senior SCADA engineering with functional service leadership and does not include personnel line management. You will personally undertake engineering work while coordinating and prioritising the service team’s activities, monitoring outcomes and making risks, dependencies and resource needs visible. Capability and capacity requirements will be aligned with the Asset Service Area OT O&M Manager, with resources requested from the respective line managers.

You will apply your practical engineering expertise to diagnose faults, restore services and implement controlled technical changes within your agreed scope and authorisation. You will provide technical guidance to colleagues, assess operational risks and challenge proposed solutions, combining hands-on delivery with effective planning and coordination across organisational boundaries.

You will participate in the team’s on-call rotation, personally diagnosing and resolving incidents affecting SCADA and Power Plant Control services outside normal working hours, within your agreed technical scope and authorisation. You will involve other engineers, OEMs and suppliers when specialist support is required, follow agreed escalation arrangements and contribute to root-cause investigations and corrective and preventive actions.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Service scope and support arrangements: Maintaining clear service definitions, ownership boundaries, agreed service levels, support responsibilities and escalation arrangements, aligned with the agreed service mapping, the Asset Service Area OT O&M Manager and customer expectations.

• Service delivery and hands-on engineering: Managing reliable, secure and efficient day-to-day delivery of SCADA and Power Plant Control services, including monitoring, incidents, service requests, problems, changes and lifecycle activities. Personally configuring, testing, commissioning, maintaining and improving assigned systems, controllers and interfaces within approved procedures and authorisations, while balancing engineering assignments with service-leadership responsibilities and agreed priorities.

• Service performance: Monitoring performance against agreed service-level agreements (SLAs), key performance indicators (KPIs) and operational targets. Reporting on service availability, incident response and restoration, recurring issues, risks and improvement actions.

• Incident response and problem management: Personally diagnosing and resolving incidents affecting assigned SCADA systems, Power Plant Control systems and interfaces, while coordinating additional engineers, OEMs, suppliers and support functions as required. Ensuring timely service restoration and clear stakeholder updates, investigating root causes and implementing or assigning corrective and preventive actions, with follow-up to completion.

• Backlog and delivery planning: Managing and prioritising the service team’s backlog, dependencies and delivery plans based on higher-level guidance, operational impact, risk and available capacity. Planning your own engineering assignments alongside service-leadership responsibilities, balancing urgent operational needs with planned maintenance, lifecycle work and improvements, and making capacity trade-offs visible.

• Capability and capacity planning: Identifying the skills and capacity required to deliver agreed services and roadmap commitments, aligning them with the Asset Service Area OT O&M Manager, and requesting resources from the respective line managers and making the consequences of resource gaps visible.

• Lifecycle engineering and controlled change: Executing the agreed service roadmap through hands-on engineering and coordination of upgrades, migrations, patching, configuration changes and lifecycle replacements. Preparing, implementing or reviewing assigned changes, with appropriate risk assessment, testing, rollback arrangements, documentation and operational handover through approved processes.

• Supplier and stakeholder coordination: Coordinating contributions from suppliers, specialists and internal support functions, monitoring delivery against agreed responsibilities and service commitments, and following up on issues. Supporting technical and service-related purchasing or contract discussions with the responsible procurement and contract owners.

• Project requirements and transition to operations: Providing OT operations and maintenance requirements to projects whose deliverables will enter the service team’s scope. Agreeing operational acceptance criteria with the relevant stakeholders and participating in readiness reviews and handovers, checking support coverage, monitoring, documentation, recovery arrangements and unresolved risks.

• Operational documentation and knowledge: Producing and maintaining technical records, configuration information, operational runbooks and troubleshooting guidance for your own engineering work. Ensuring that the service team maintains relevant service and asset records, clear support responsibilities, escalation arrangements and accessible operational knowledge.

• Continual improvement and technical guidance: Using service-performance data and operational experience to identify, prioritise and implement improvements that reduce recurring incidents and strengthen reliability, efficiency and supportability. Standardising repeatable services and work packages, contributing to technical reviews, and supporting colleagues through practical guidance, knowledge sharing and appropriate automation.

• Security, compliance and audit support: Ensuring that applicable cybersecurity, regulatory and operational requirements are incorporated into service delivery and lifecycle planning, in collaboration with the responsible service engineers, cybersecurity and compliance functions. Coordinating relevant evidence and follow-up actions for audits and reviews.

• Risk management and escalation: Maintaining visibility of service risks, dependencies, delivery constraints and outstanding decisions. Escalating issues beyond the service team’s mandate or capacity to the Asset Service Area OT O&M Manager and other responsible stakeholders, with clear recommendations and operational consequences.

Your profile / who are you?

You hold a relevant bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, automation or control engineering, computer engineering, industrial IT, systems engineering or a related discipline. Alternatively, you have developed equivalent professional competence through a relevant technical qualification and substantial hands-on experience in SCADA or industrial OT engineering and operational support.

You have several years of hands-on experience engineering, operating and supporting SCADA systems or comparable industrial OT solutions, including recent practical experience diagnosing faults, restoring services and implementing controlled changes. You can personally diagnose faults, restore services and implement controlled technical changes. You have also demonstrated the ability to coordinate technical work, prioritise operational needs and guide colleagues or suppliers. Your background may be as a senior engineer, technical lead or service manager who has remained technically active; a previous formal Service Manager title is not required.

You understand the demands of supporting business-critical systems and can translate operational needs into clear priorities, responsibilities and delivery plans. You are comfortable taking responsibility for service outcomes while working with engineers, suppliers and line managers in a matrix organisation.

You have excellent written and spoken English skills and can communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders. The role may be subject to security clearance, and candidates must be able to meet the applicable screening requirements.

You bring knowledge and experience in:

• Operational service management: Applying structured incident, problem, service-request, change, configuration and lifecycle-management practices, with clear ownership, service levels and follow-up.

• Hands-on SCADA engineering: Practical experience configuring, integrating, testing, commissioning, maintaining, operating and supporting SCADA systems and interfaces, including documenting and validating technical changes.

• SCADA and OT environments: Understanding the role of SCADA in asset monitoring and control, including interfaces and dependencies between WTG and substation systems, power plant control, central control systems and supporting infrastructure. You can engage meaningfully with specialists and assess the operational implications of technical proposals.

• Service leadership and prioritisation: Coordinating multidisciplinary service teams and suppliers, managing backlogs and dependencies, identifying capacity requirements and resolving competing priorities within an agreed mandate.

• Operational resilience and secure engineering: Practical experience supporting service availability through monitoring, backup and recovery of SCADA applications and configurations, secure access, vulnerability handling and controlled technical changes, in collaboration with the teams responsible for supporting infrastructure.

• Service introduction and handover: Translating operations and maintenance needs into project requirements and acceptance criteria, assessing operational readiness and coordinating the transition of new or changed solutions into supported services.

• Supplier and stakeholder management: Establishing clear expectations, following up on service commitments, coordinating across organisational boundaries and handling escalations constructively.

• Incident and problem management: Diagnosing faults across SCADA applications, Power Plant Control systems, interfaces and connected systems, including dependencies on server services, networks, certificates and service accounts. Personally restoring services within your technical scope and authorisation, investigating root causes and implementing corrective and preventive actions, with specialist or supplier support where required.

• Performance analysis and improvement: Using service metrics, incident trends, risks and operational feedback to identify improvement priorities, track actions and communicate progress and results.

Additional experience that would be valuable:

• Experience with wind-turbine and substation SCADA platforms, hybrid park controllers, or OEM-specific WTG Power Plant Controllers and their interfaces.

• ITIL or comparable service-management training, or relevant OT cybersecurity training.

• Experience with service-management, backlog-planning, reporting and knowledge-management tools.

Personal traits

To succeed in this role, we believe that you:

• Take ownership of service outcomes and follow through on commitments, decisions and improvement actions.

• Lead through clear priorities, constructive challenge and collaboration, including where you do not have direct line authority.

• Remain calm and decisive during operational incidents, communicating clearly and involving the right people at the right time.

• Work in a structured and transparent way, making risks, dependencies, resource constraints and delivery progress visible.

• Use sound judgement to balance immediate service restoration, operational risk, long-term reliability, maintainability and agreed delivery priorities.

• Build effective relationships across engineering, Operations, projects, suppliers and support functions, and actively encourage knowledge sharing.

We look forward to receiving your application!

Location: Kolding, Denmark or Amsterdam, Netherlands

Additional Information

Our offer

Looking for a career with growth?

Looking for a role where your superpowers can be leveraged to the maximum and with limitless opportunities for growth?

The scale and ambition of our wind, battery and solar business means you can

At Intempus, our goal is simple: make time tracking as easy, intelligent and automated as it can possibly be. We're building the future of time tracking and our ambitions are high. This means that our system needs to deliver a stable and great user experience at all times — especially since our user base keeps growing fast.

That’s why we're looking for you: an experienced DevOps Engineer ready for the challenge.

What we offer

• 
A role where you can grow, learn and make a real impact

• 
A helpful, social and diverse workplace with a flat hierarchy and open communication

• 
A healthy work/life balance

• 
55 friendly, driven and skilled colleagues

• 
Flexibility, including two days of remote work per week

• 
A centrally located, modern office at Visma House in Carlsberg Byen, Copenhagen

•

Your role

• 
Automate infrastructure and server configuration using tools like Ansible, Terraform or whatever fits best — we're moving from a fully manual setup to infrastructure and configuration that's fully documented and managed as code

• 
Monitor and troubleshoot day-to-day issues across our servers and applications

• 
Design and implement improvements using the best tools the DevOps ecosystem has to offer — anything from a new secrets management solution to better container deployment workflows

• 
Collaborate with developers to improve tooling around development and test environments

• 
Keep our infrastructure and applications updated and secure

•

Who are you?

You're proactive and take ownership of your work. You thrive in a team with plenty of freedom, where ideas are shared openly and people genuinely listen to and support each other.

You communicate clearly, both in writing and in person, and you actively help foster a good team environment.

You hold a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or equivalent, and you bring at least 7 years of experience in a DevOps role or similar (e.g. System Administrator).

On the technical side, you have experience with:

• 
Managing Linux systems for at least two years (we run Debian-based Linux across all our servers)

• 
Bash scripting — you're comfortable working in a bash shell

• 
Docker — building, testing, deploying and maintaining containerized applications in production

• 
A programming language (our CI/CD pipeline and much of our automation is written in Python)

• 
git

An infrastructure-as-code tool, ideally Terraform

A configuration management tool, ideally Ansible

Container orchestration (e.g. Kubernetes, HashiCorp Nomad)

Nice to have, but not required:

Managing PostgreSQL databases

• 
Cloud services with any provider

Who are we?

Intempus is a Danish software company with offices in Copenhagen and Aarhus. Since 2012, we've built, refined and optimized our own time-tracking system, and we continue to hold high ambitions for our product.

Our team of 55 includes a development team of 35 driven engineers. We are part of the Visma Group but operate day-to-day as an independent company.

Take a look at our team in the Copenhagen office here!

Ready to join us?

Apply now if you can see yourself as our new DevOps Engineer. Job start is January 1st, 2027, but we are flexible for the right candidate. The role is on-site at our office at Visma House in Carlsberg Byen, Copenhagen.

Please submit your application in English, as we are an international team, and include your resumé, educational diploma and references.

We look forward to hearing from you!

In this role, you will be responsible for driving an integrated marketing strategy that strengthens our brand, engages customers and employees, supports commercial growth, and delivers measurable business impact.

As part of the Danish Marketing Leadership Team, you will lead a team of five employees and collaborate closely with stakeholders across Sales, Marketing, Finance, and regional and global teams. **

jobs.description:
Job Description

Do you want to help shape how a large IT company measures, manages and documents its information security? Are you motivated by turning data, risk and regulation into practical decisions? If so, you may be our next colleague in the newly established GRC team in Netcompany's Group CISO Office.

Responsibilities and technologies

As a member of the GRC team, you will help ensure that Netcompany has an accurate, data-driven view of the effectiveness of its security controls and its level of compliance. The team takes a pragmatic and technically grounded approach to governance, risk and compliance, and works closely with the Application Security team, the Operations organisation, Internal IT and other business functions across the group.

The GRC team is a small team of colleagues with complementary profiles. We do not expect any one candidate to cover every area described below. Instead, we are looking for broad profiles with solid experience across several of these areas and the motivation to develop within the rest.

Your responsibilites will typically include:

• Developing and maintaining risk scenarios, assessing the effectiveness of mitigating controls against the scenarios, and conducting risk assessments to support business decisions

• Establishing automated measurements and KPIs that provide insight into the implementation and effectiveness of security controls across the business

• Interpreting regulatory and contractual security requirements and translating these into Netcompany's security baselines and standard methodologies

• Planning and executing security awareness activities, including phishing simulations, targeted micro-learning, and onboarding/yearly awareness training

• Driving smaller security improvement projects from planning to implementation, combining coordination with hands-on execution

• Developing, maintaining and testing internal security processes, such as major incident response, crisis management and business continuityDeveloping, maintaining and testing internal security processes, such as major incident response, crisis management and business continuity

About you

You have broad experience within information security and a solid understanding of its technical aspects alongside a general understanding of the software development life cycle. You combine this with the ability to translate regulatory requirements into practical solutions. Furthermore, you are pragmatic, take ownership of your work and prefer a hands-on approach.

To succeed in this role you:

• Hold a relevant degree or equivalent experience; within IT, engineering, computer science or a similar field.

• Strong analytic skills, with the ability to interpret data and draw meaningful conclusions independently.

• Experience within several of the areas listed in the overview of responsibilities in the role.

• Solid communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to engage effectively with technical teams, business functions, management and, on occasion, customers.

• Full professional proficiency in Danish and English (written and spoken).

Continue developing with us

At Netcompany, we focus on your personal and professional development.

We provide a structured career model that allows you to build on your existing experiences.

When you join us, you will be assigned a personal mentor who will support your development and help you achieve your personal and professional goals. The close relationship with an experienced colleague in management gives you concrete insights into the various business areas and responsibilities that match your interests and desires.

Additionally, you will be enrolled in our internal training programme, Netcompany Academy, where you are offered courses and seminars tailored to you and where you are in your career. As part of our culture and values, all employees, regardless of background, identity, and experience, are met with understanding and respect and given equal opportunities for development and well-being.

As we are an international company with offices in many countries, you will have the opportunity to learn and collaborate internationally with colleagues from across the world. We offer a shared environment where we engage with each other across departments and projects. Additionally, we have a wide range of social and professional events that provide you with the best opportunities to expand your network.

Send us an application

**Do you want to help ensure quality in energy infrastructure projects? Can you turn quality requirements into practical activities and support projects through to handover? And do you have experience with quality management, audits and inspections? Then join COWI as our new Quality Consultant.

****Create the solutions that will enable a better tomorrow

**We are looking for a Quality Consultant to join COWI and support our customers’ construction and operational projects on assignments of both shorter and longer duration. You will help ensure that projects follow the customer’s governance framework and can be handed over to the operations organisation at the required quality level, with all supporting documentation. Your work may span electricity transmission projects, including cables, overhead lines and substations; gas distribution and transmission networks, including natural gas and biogas facilities and stations; oil pipelines; and gas storage facilities.

Your key responsibilities will be:

• Support projects in applying internal processes and tools and provide guidance and support on quality-related matters.

• Consistently promote and embed quality management in projects so that documentation, products and deliverables meet the specified requirements

• Plan, carry out and document the necessary quality activities in collaboration with the project team, including internal and external audits and inspections of project partners.

• Ensure that quality-related experience and lessons learned are shared within the customer’s organisation.

• Prepare project quality plans.

**Your skills. Our team. Together we design the future.

**The first step to success in this role is that you are eager to collaborate with the people around you, whether they are colleagues, partners or customers. Developing ties with others is something you do by acting respectfully and delivering on your promises. And you never get set in your ways, but keep exploring new insights and ways to improve.

You work in a structured and systematic way and take a proactive approach to building relationships. You collaborate and communicate on an equal footing with internal and external stakeholders involved in construction projects. You bring professional credibility in your field and can work independently.

On top of that, you will have:

• An understanding of the structure and application of quality management systems.

• Experience with project- and process-related work.

• Experience with quality management activities in infrastructure and construction projects, including quality assurance (QA) and providing input to quality control (QC) activities.

• Experience carrying out quality activities, including audits and inspections of internal and external parties involved in projects.

• Experience using the Microsoft Office suite.

• The ability to communicate in Danish and English, both orally and in writing, at negotiation level.

Your official COWI office location will be either Lyngby, Vejle or Aarhus. However, your primary workplace will be at Energinet in Erritsø, but Ballerup could also be an option, with some travel to Erritsø. You will report to Head of Discipline, Ioana Nicoleta Tuglui, who is based at COWI's headquarters in Lyngby.

**A place to work and so much more

**At COWI, we work together with our customers to shape a sustainable and liveable world. We do it by applying our knowledge and curiosity – and sometimes even our courage – to create the solutions the world needs today to enable a better tomorrow. We support our customers’ transition towards increased sustainability. We strive to lead by example by embedding environmental management, social responsibility and good governance into our business practices and the options we provide to our customers.

We value differences and development and cultivate an environment of belonging and having fun. Because that is what brings out the best in you, at work and at home.

With offices primarily located in the Nordic region, the UK, North America and India, we are currently more than 7,500 people who bring their expertise in engineering, architecture, energy and environment into play.

Get to know us even better at our website, www.cowi.com, where you can learn more about our projects, our strategy, what we want to achieve and what life is like at COWI.

**Before you apply

**All you need to include in your application is your CV – no photo or application letter. At an interview, you can tell us everything we need to know about why you’re interested in joining COWI. As for the photo, we prefer to form our first impression in person rather than from a picture.

**Diversity is fundamental to COWI, inclusion is key

**We are committed to creating a respectful and fair work environment where all employees have a sense of belonging and equitable opportunities to thrive and grow. We ensure that our leaders are role models for inclusive leadership by cultivating a culture where diverse perspectives and thoughts are seen as strengths. And we take diversity and inclusion into account in all relevant decisions and processes and when setting teams and fora. We do it because it is part of our values and because it is simply the right thing to do.

Looking for a workplace where you can make real change? A meaningful job where you have the freedom, trust and responsibilities to play an important role and not just be a small fish in a big shoal? Does being a part of a social, passionate, and international team sound right to you? Join us!

Your position

In your new position as a Telecom & Network Engineer in the Telecom Engineering Department, you will join a multicultural, diverse team of skilled, enthusiastic telecommunication specialists from all over the world. Ibsen Photonics develops Spectral Beam Combining (SBC) modules for high-power laser architectures, based on our in-house transmission gratings. • Knowledge of opto-mechanical design practices for high-power devices

• Hands-on experience with precise free-space and/or fibre optical alignment and experimental troubleshooting

• Experience with beam quality measurement and analysis

• Professional proficiency in English

Nice to have

• Experience with SBC or CBC techniques

• Mechanical design of tight-tolerance devices and familiarity with mechanical CAD

BWSC is seeking a highly skilled and motivated Senior Legal Counsel to join our legal team in Allerød, Denmark. In this role, you will play a key part in managing legal matters across the business, ensuring compliance with applicable laws and regulations, and providing practical, strategic legal guidance to our business units. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to an international company with a global reach and a strong focus on sustainable energy solutions.

BWSC – Ever better energy!

Join us in our mission in building a world of sustainable energy and making a meaningful impact on the world of power generation and energy conversion.

BWSC is a leading player in the power generation industry, specializing in the service, operations, and maintenance of power plants. We are seeking to always provide Ever Better Energy whether it comes to optimizing a conventional power plant, operating a biomass power plant or constructing new energy facilities. Our commitment to excellence, innovation, and environmental stewardship sets us apart in the industry.

The position

As Senior Legal Counsel, you will be part of BWSC’s legal team and report directly to the General Counsel. You will work closely with management and key stakeholders across the organization, providing legal advice that supports BWSC’s commercial activities, corporate governance and strategic priorities.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Providing expert legal advice on a wide range of topics, including contract law, commercial transactions, corporate governance, company law, and dispute resolution.

• Drafting, reviewing, and negotiating contracts and agreements that are critical to our projects, partnerships, and business operations.

• Identifying and mitigating legal risks by conducting thorough risk assessments and advising on effective strategies.

• Supporting corporate governance efforts, ensuring compliance with local and international regulations, company policies, and corporate structures.

• Collaborating with external legal counsel on specialized legal issues and complex cases.

• Staying ahead of legal developments by monitoring relevant legislation, industry regulations, and trends to ensure BWSC’s compliance.

• Managing dispute resolution processes, including litigation and arbitration, to protect the company’s interests.

• Educating internal teams on legal matters, such as contract management, compliance, and corporate policies, to foster a culture of legal awareness.

Qualifications

At BWSC, we believe that our people are the foundation of our success. As Senior Legal Counsel, you will bring solid legal expertise, sound business judgement and the ability to navigate complex legal matters in close collaboration with internal stakeholders.

The ideal candidate thrives in an international environment, works independently and has the following background and experience:

• Holds a Danish Master of Laws degree or equivalent legal qualification.

• Possesses a strong understanding of Danish law and relevant international legal frameworks, with experience in cross-border transactions and dispute resolution.

• Is fluent in Danish and English, both written and spoken.

• Has at least 5 years of legal experience, preferably in-house or with a law firm, specializing in commercial contracts, corporate law, or the energy/industrial sector.

• Demonstrates excellent drafting and negotiation skills with attention to detail.

• Exhibits strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.

• Can work independently, manage multiple tasks, and prioritize effectively.

• Shows a high degree of professionalism, integrity, and the ability to collaborate with management, clients, and external partners.

What do we offer?

At BWSC, you will have the opportunity to work in an international company that values innovation, collaboration and personal development. We offer flexible working conditions and an inspiring work environment where you can make a real difference.

We have a good canteen, fitness facilities and an active Staff Club that contributes with various events and activities. Our HQ is located in Allerød, close to the train station and only a 30-minute ride from central Copenhagen.

We look forward to hearing from you

We look forward to receiving your application. If you have any questions regarding the position, please do not hesitate to contact Nicolai Lygum at nily@bwsc.dk.

BWSC wants to promote equality and diversity. We encourage all qualified candidates to apply - regardless of ethnic background, gender, sexual orientation, disability, religion, or age. We therefore recommend not stating age etc. on application documents.

Get to know us even better at our website, www.bwsc.com, where you can learn more about our projects, our strategy and what we want to achieve at BWSC.

Burmeister & Wain Scandinavian Contractor A/S (BWSC) is a global power plant Operation & Maintenance and technical service provider with engineering expertise, enabling power plant owners to deliver cleaner and affordable energy. We are experts in servicing, upgrading, operating, and maintaining energy systems for diesel, natural gas, and renewable baseload power plants worldwide. We help our customers increase reliability and availability of energy production, improve efficiency and performance of their power plant, design and integrate future-proof technologies, and secure lower cost of maintenance.

Our people are at the core of everything we do and key to building strong relationships with our customers. **Intro

**Monta powers the EV charging ecosystem. With 300,000+ monthly users and millions of charge sessions every month, our platform accelerates the electrification of mobility.

This is a fast-moving place. The problems are hard, the pace is quick, and the bar is high. If you like real ownership, figuring things out, and seeing the direct impact of your work, you'll do well with us.

AI is built into how we work. It helps us ship faster, make better decisions, and stay lean. Everyone at Monta is expected to use AI tools thoughtfully — and to find smart ways to use them to move the work forward.

Our principles keep us grounded: Build Together & Finish, Sweat the Details, Customer First, and Aim for the Moon.

The best part of Monta is the people — sharp, ambitious, and good to be around. You'll be challenged, supported, and trusted to deliver.

We're looking for a Solution Engineer who's ready to roll up their sleeves, take ownership, and build with us — through the grind and the wins. You'll be the technical partner to our Sales team: you work out what customers need, show them how Monta solves it, and make sure what we sell can be delivered.

**This Is What You Will Achieve

**

• Win the technical decision — be the reason charge point operators, energy companies and fleet owners choose Monta to run their charging business.

• Make sure what we sell gets delivered — the commitments made during the sale are realistic and land cleanly with our implementation team.

• Shape the product — turn what you hear from customers into clear input that Product and Engineering can act on.

**What You Will Do

**

• Lead technical discovery — understand the customer's business, their current charging setup (platform, hardware, roaming, billing) and what they need to integrate with.

• Run demos built around the customer — tailored to their use cases, not a feature tour.

• Design the solution — define the high-level architecture and integration approach, from OCPP chargers and OCPI roaming to APIs, ERP and energy management.

• Lead proofs of concept and technical evaluations — agree scope and success criteria up front and see them through to sign-off.

• Answer the hard questions — technical, architecture, integration and security questions in meetings, RFPs and security questionnaires.

• Spot risk early — flag gaps and dependencies before a deal is committed, and push back when a promise can't be kept.

• Partner with Sales — on the technical strategy for complex, multi-country deals.

• Hand over cleanly — give the Solution Architect a documented scope so implementation starts on solid ground.

• Close the loop with Product — feed recurring requirements and product gaps back to Product and Engineering.

• Help post-sales when it's busy — for example scoping a migration or running a technical workshop with a live customer.

**What We're Looking For

**

• Experience in a customer-facing technical role — as a Solution Engineer, Sales Engineer or pre-sales consultant, selling B2B software or platform products.

• You explain technical topics clearly to non-technical people — and can go deep with the customer's engineers in the same meeting.

• Your discovery gets to the real problem — you ask the question behind the requirement before proposing a solution.

• You build demos that tell the customer's story — you're comfortable changing course live when the conversation goes somewhere new.

• Hands-on with APIs and integrations — you can read API docs, test calls yourself, and explain web-hooks, authentication and data flows.

• Commercial awareness — you understand how deals are won and lost, and you know when to protect scope.

• You write clearly — solution designs, RFP answers and handover notes that others can act on without a follow-up call.

• EV charging, energy or mobility knowledge is a plus (OCPP, OCPI, load management), but not required. We'll teach you the domain.

• You use AI to work faster — for example on RFP drafts, research, demo prep and documentation, and you check the output before it reaches a customer.

• Fluent English, and happy to travel to customer workshops around Europe from time to time.

**_If the mission excites you but your experience isn't a perfect 1:1 match, apply anyway — we care about potential, not perfection.

_****Why Monta

**

• Impact, not easy mode — your work matters, and you'll feel it every day.

• Ownership from day one — we don't micromanage, we expect you to deliver.

• The grind is real — priorities shift, and flexibility is sometimes needed to get things across the finish line. But so are the rewards: impact, growth, and a team that has your back.

• The people are extraordinary — talented, driven, and fun to work with. You'll be challenged, supported, and inspired in equal measure.

**What We Offer

**

• A yearly education budget and extra days off to use it.

• A friendly and social company culture with movie nights, Friday bars, pub crawls, and more.

• Free lunch every day.

• Pension & health coverage to keep you secure for today and tomorrow.

• Paid parental leave to support life's big moments.

• Warrants program - be part of our growth story.

• Flexible working hours; as long as you're at key meetings and delivering great work, we trust you to manage your schedule.

**Please send us your application in English.

**To succeed in this position, your spoken and written English skills need to be proficient. Since Monta is a globally active company, you'll be communicating often and regularly with our co-workers and partners around the world, making your professional English knowledge essential.

_Recently graduated or one to two years into your career? Join us and work with critical data in Markets as part of a team that is being built right now.

__Join us in building a new data capability in Markets

**About The Job

**At Saxo, we are building the Markets Data Office as part of our Data Governance Programme. The team is organised across four domain areas: Products, Operations, Counterparty Risk and Market Risk. Together, these areas reflect how critical data is used across Markets.

We are a newly established team and still in our build phase. Our first permanent colleagues joined in September 2026. Today, we are eight people, and we are growing to twelve.

As the team grows, we are creating the foundations for how we work, including frameworks, standards, tooling and governance practices. At the same time, we are already delivering on ongoing data initiatives across Markets.

This is an opportunity to join early, learn quickly and help shape how we work.

**What You Will Do

**As a Data Portfolio Analyst, you will work within one of our four domain areas together with business stakeholders, data owners, data stewards and technology teams. Your focus will be on improving how critical data is defined, monitored and controlled.

Depending on your domain, you could work with instrument reference data, market data, price data, custody information, election data, trades, positions, counterparty risk or model data.

You will learn about Markets from experienced colleagues and gradually take responsibility for your own tasks. At the same time, you will be part of one Markets Data Office with shared standards, tooling and governance practices.

**Your Responsibilities Will Include

**

• Helping identify and document Critical Data Attributes (CDAs) by reviewing data points with stakeholders and assessing which are critical for Saxo

• Analysing data together with data owners to assess quality, identify issues and contribute to root cause investigations

• Helping define and maintain data definitions, rules, thresholds and supporting documentation

• Monitoring data quality outputs, following up on remediation and raising issues when they are not being resolved

• Collaborating with data owners, data stewards and stakeholders across business and technology

• Contributing to the frameworks, standards and ways of working for the Markets Data Office

A key part of your role will be making sure documentation is clear, structured and easy to maintain. This helps create transparency and consistency across the organisation.

**Who You Are

**You have recently graduated or have around one to two years of professional experience.

**We Imagine That You Bring

**

• A relevant degree in finance, economics, business analytics, information systems, data science or a similar field

• An interest in data and how it is used in business processes

• Experience with SQL, Python or similar tools from your studies, a student job or projects

• Hands on experience using AI and other technology tools to automate tasks and find smarter ways of working

• Good communication skills in English and the ability to write clear and structured documentation

**It would be an advantage if you have

**

• Experience from banking or financial services, for example through a student job

• Knowledge of, or an interest in, Markets functions such as trading, risk, investment products or operations, including how a trade moves from front to back

• Exposure to data governance or data quality work such as data profiling, data controls or data lineage, ideally within financial services

• Familiarity with Databricks, Great Expectations, OpenMetadata or similar tools

Just as important as your experience is how you approach your work.

**We Are Looking For Someone Who

**

• Takes ownership. You move your work forward, follow through and take initiative.

• Collaborates naturally. You build relationships with business stakeholders, technology teams and colleagues across different domain areas.

• Uses technology naturally. You use technology to analyse, automate, document and find more effective ways of working.

• Is comfortable working in an evolving environment. You adapt as priorities develop, bring structure to areas that are still taking shape and contribute to building solutions together with the team.

• Is structured and curious. You have a strong analytical mindset, pay attention to detail and enjoy understanding how things work.

You do not need to know everything from day one. What matters most is your curiosity, initiative and willingness to learn.

**What We Offer

**

• The opportunity to help build a new data function from the ground up

• A steep learning curve across Markets, critical data and data governance, supported by experienced colleagues

• Hands on guidance, regular feedback and an introduction to both your Markets domain and our governance practices

• Real responsibility from the beginning, with the opportunity to take on more as you develop

You will join the Markets Data Office at an early stage of its journey, so your role will develop alongside the team. You can expect new challenges, increasing responsibility and the opportunity to influence how critical data is managed across Markets.

**We get curious people invested in the world

**When you work at Saxo, you become a Saxonian and part of a purpose-driven organisation, where good ideas are always taken seriously, and where you can make a true impact. We are invested in your development, and you can expect a robust career from day one when you join Saxo – no matter which role you take on.

You will join 2,500 other ambitious colleagues across 11 countries and become part of an international organisation. Working in Saxo, you will get to meet colleagues from many different cultures and backgrounds, and you should know that we value diversity and inclusion and see it as a genuine source of strength to drive growth, foster innovation and position us for long-term success.

We encourage an open feedback culture and supportive team environments enabling employees to grow and fulfil their career aspirations.

When you bring passion, curiosity, drive and team spirit, your learning journey will be dynamic and your career opportunities in Saxo will be immense.

At Saxo we don’t just offer a job – we offer an opportunity to invest in your future!

**How To Apply

**Click here to create an account and upload your resume and a short motivation. We look forward to getting to know you better!
